gaps.recommendation: Stop extruding boxes. Build each road as one triangle strip: sample the terrain at every cross-section vertex (left edge, centre, right edge) at ~4 m spacing and lift by a constant 0.06 m, so the ribbon conforms continuously. Cheaper alternative that also kills the hard edge: drop road geometry entirely and paint the road into the terrain vertex colours during the terrain build (the loop already computes colorAt per vertex), plus a darker roughness — zero extra draw calls and no z-fighting.

gaps.gap: Sunlight shadows stop 55 m from the camera; the other ~99% of the visible world is unshadowed
gaps.evidence: ffg_royale3d.js applyGraphics(): SHADOW_EXT = { low: 55, medium: 55, high: 70 }, sun.shadow.camera far 400, volume slid to follow the player. Final Drop, read live: sun numCascades 4, shadowResolution 4096, shadowDistance 700. In my rendered Coco Village frame not one building casts a shadow onto the ground, so structures look pasted onto the terrain rather than sitting on it.
gaps.recommendation: Swap the single shadow camera for three.js's own cascaded shadow maps — `three/addons/csm/CSM.js` is already reachable through the existing importmap (three/addons/ -> jsDelivr three@0.172.0/examples/jsm/), no build change. Practical split mode, 3 cascades on medium (1024/1024/1024) and 4 on high (2048 near), maxFar ~400 m. Keep the existing bias/normalBias and drop followShadow(), which CSM replaces.

gaps.gap: Every building in the game is an untextured box — no windows, doors, pitched roofs, or detail geometry
gaps.evidence: maps.js: hut(), house(), tower(), rangerTower(), lighthouse(), waterTower(), steeple(), farmland() are all composed exclusively of addBox()/addRamp() calls, merged into one mesh per hex colour with a single shared 256 px brick/panel CanvasTexture at STRUCT_TILE 2.6 m. Doors are a gap between two wall boxes; roofs are a flat slab plus a ridge-cap box. My Ashgrid 'Downtown Core' render shows six identical tan prisms on a flat plain — that is the map's densest POI. Final Drop uses Synty POLYGON kits (PolygonTown_01_A/_Glass, PolygonBattleRoyale_01_A, PolygonMilitary_01_A) across 159 prefab templa
gaps.recommendation: Replace the box generators with a modular prefab kit and keep the generators only as placement logic. Kenney's CC0 City/Survival/Modular-Building kits or an equivalent Synty-style low-poly pack gives wall/door/window/roof/stair modules that snap on a grid — the existing addBox call sites become 'place module at (x,y,z,rot)'. Start with the ~8 modules that cover 80% of placements (wall, wall-with-window, wall-with-door, floor, flat roof, pitched roof, stair, railing). Collision can stay as the current AABBs.

gaps.gap: Terrain is 7.27 m per vertex, one un-chunked mesh, with zero ground clutter or contact darkening
gaps.evidence: maps.js: SIZE 1600, SEG 220 -> 7.27 m/vertex, 96,800 triangles in a single always-submitted PlaneGeometry; the only surface detail is a 256 px near-white grain texture tiled every 8 m at normalScale 0.55. The grid stairstep is visible on the volcano silhouette in my Isla Viva aerial, and in the Deepwood snow render the ground is a featureless pale sheet with faint grazing-angle streaks. Final Drop carries 863 LOD entities, a Ground Contact Blend system, and lightmapMaxResolution 2048.
gaps.recommendation: Two changes, both affordable given the measured 36-198 draw calls. (1) Chunk the terrain into a 8x8 grid of 200 m tiles at ~3 m/vertex near the player and 12 m/vertex beyond ~300 m — same total triangle budget, four times the near-field silhouette fidelity, and per-chunk frustum culling for free. (2) Add an instanced ground-clutter layer (grass tufts, pebbles, fallen branches, 3 GLBs, ~2,000 instances) refreshed in a 60 m ring around the player; this is the single highest visual-return-per-triangle change available and would fill the empty green expanses that dominate every frame I captured.

gaps.gap: Sky-islands — the signature feature — render as solid black cones
gaps.evidence: maps.js sky-island block: the hanging rock is ConeGeometry(rad*0.9, rad*1.5, 8) with MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x7a6a58, roughness: 1 }), rotated 180 degrees so its lit surfaces face down. With only a HemisphereLight groundColor (#7c8672) reaching the underside, it renders near-black. In my Deepwood forest render and my Ashgrid downtown render the islands read as flat black triangles hanging in the sky.
gaps.recommendation: Three cheap fixes together: lighten the rock to ~#9a8a75, raise the material's contribution from below by giving the island group its own tiny non-shadowing PointLight or by adding a vertex-colour gradient that brightens toward the tip, and raise the cone to 12-16 radial segments so it silhouettes as rock rather than a party hat. Even simpler: set the cone material's emissive to a 0.06-strength tint of the map's sky colour so the underside picks up skylight.

gaps.gap: Fog density is set so low there is no aerial perspective — the horizon is as saturated as your feet
gaps.evidence: maps.js MAPS: fog 0.00042 / 0.00045 / 0.00052 on FogExp2. At d=800 m and density 0.00045 the fog factor is 1-exp(-(0.36)^2) = 0.12, i.e. 12% blend. In my Ashgrid render a POI roughly 700 m out is fully saturated; in the Isla Viva aerial the whole island reads as one flat colour plate with a hard horizon line. Final Drop runs exp2 fog through a dedicated uranus-effects-environment-fog.js with a light blue-white fog colour.
gaps.recommendation: Raise density to ~0.0018-0.0022 (about 75% blend at 800 m, 25% at 300 m) and set the fog colour to the sky dome's HORIZON colour rather than the flat sky key, so distant terrain dissolves into the skyline instead of cutting against it. Add a simple height falloff if you want the volcano peak to stay crisp while the coastline hazes.

gaps.gap: Ashgrid's sky is graded as dusk over noon-lit ground
gaps.evidence: maps.js sky block: zenith = new THREE.Color(K.sky).lerp(new THREE.Color(0x2f74c8), 0.55).multiplyScalar(0.9). With ashgrid's K.sky = '#e7cf98' (tan), that yields a dark slate-navy zenith over a tan horizon, while the same map's sun runs at intensity 2.05 warm-white with a 1.25 hemisphere fill. My render shows a stormy dusk sky sitting above brightly lit noon savanna — the two halves of the frame disagree.
gaps.recommendation: Author the zenith colour per map as an explicit constant next to `sky` in the MAPS table instead of deriving it, and pick it to be consistent with the sun angle: for a golden savanna, a warm pale blue (~#8fb8d8) at zenith over #e7cf98 at horizon. Same treatment for the other two maps so each biome gets a deliberate two-colour sky ramp.

gaps.gap: No LOD and no foliage billboards — density can never be raised without a cliff
gaps.evidence: Grep for LOD across runtime/3d returns only animation-mixer LOD in player.js; every prop is a full-detail InstancedMesh with all instances always submitted. Measured 1,565,770 triangles on the Deepwood aerial and 1,579,272 in the forest interior, at only 36-56 draw calls — the triangles are all trees, at full detail, at any distance. Final Drop runs 863 LOD entities (LOD0/1/2 chains) plus a dedicated billboard_vegetation_atlas.png and MI_FirTree4_Billboard.
gaps.recommendation: Add a two-tier system per tree kind: the existing GLB inside ~90 m, and a two-quad cross-billboard (one 512 px atlas, alphaTest) beyond it, both as InstancedMesh with the instance split recomputed on a 1 Hz timer around the player. That typically drops foliage triangles 8-10x and buys the budget to roughly triple tree counts — which is what the sparse aerials actually need.

gaps.gap: Tone mapping is disabled, so bright surfaces clip flat
gaps.evidence: maps.js buildMap: `kn.renderer.toneMapping = THREE.NoToneMapping; kn.renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0;` with the comment that ACES 'was crushing + desaturating the whole scene into a muddy dusk'. Combined with player.js BODY_GAIN 3.2 (whose own calibration table records ~2.5% clipped pixels), the result is visible: in my Deepwood snow render the ground is a featureless blown white sheet, and character skin reads flat and hot in the third-person shot. Final Drop runs ACES2 (camera toneMapping 4) at exposure 0.7 and is the vibrant reference this game was chasing.
gaps.recommendation: The problem was ACES's contrast curve, not tone mapping as such. three.js r172 ships THREE.NeutralToneMapping (Khronos PBR Neutral) and THREE.AgXToneMapping — Neutral preserves saturation far better than ACES while still rolling off highlights. Switch to NeutralToneMapping at exposure ~1.15, then re-run the existing luminance calibration and expect BODY_GAIN to come down to roughly 2.4-2.7. That recovers snow texture and skin detail without going back to the muddy look.

gaps.gap: Zero local lights in the world; every emissive-looking prop is an unlit box
gaps.evidence: Grepping runtime/3d for PointLight/SpotLight finds them only in hud.js (menu fill light and the two offscreen preview scenes) — a match scene contains exactly one DirectionalLight (2.05) and one HemisphereLight (1.25). The street lamps built by streetFurniture() are addBox(lx, y+4.9, lz, 0.5, 0.3, 0.5, '#ffe9a8') with no emissive and no light. Final Drop carries 215 spot and 46 point lights including named 'Gate Light' (#ffbc00) and per-POI 'Omni Light' at intensity 6.
gaps.recommendation: Give the ~30 highest-value props a cheap emissive-plus-light treatment: set material.emissive on lamp heads, chest interiors, portal rings and supply-drop beacons, then attach a small non-shadowing PointLight (distance 12-18, decay 2) only to the nearest ~8 to the camera, recycled from a pool on a 2 Hz update. Eight extra lights costs almost nothing at the measured draw-call budget and instantly makes POIs read as places rather than props.

gaps.gap: Combat leaves no visual trace — no decals, no shell ejection
gaps.evidence: Grep for decal/blood/casing across runtime/3d returns nothing; fx.js emits only cube-particle bursts for muzzle flash, impact, explosion, hurt and death, plus DOM damage numbers. Final Drop ships a 'Material Weapon Impact Bullet', 'Material Scope Glint', 65 particle systems and a uranus-multiplayer-damage-fx.js. After a 30-round magazine into a wall, Last Circle's wall is pixel-identical to before.
gaps.recommendation: Add a pooled decal layer: 128 InstancedMesh quads with a 4-frame bullet-hole atlas, oriented to the hit normal and pushed 1 cm out along it, ring-buffered and faded over ~20 s. Reuse the surface classification weapons.js already emits (flesh/wood/stone/dirt) to pick the atlas frame, and add a scorch frame on explosion. Shell casings can ride the existing fx particle pool with a longer life and a metallic colour.

gaps.gap: Cosmetic identity is five rigs under a hue wash, against nineteen distinct outfits
gaps.evidence: player.js SKINS = ['soldier','athlete','wraith','juggernaut','viper'] with per-actor variety from color.setHSL(hue, 0.22-0.38, 0.68-0.80) * 3.2. Final Drop's container list contains 19 separate character GLBs — fish-male/female variants with braids, glasses, headphones and mustaches, plus final-drop-scifi/samurai/apocalypse male and female and four ModernPolice sets. In a 50-player lobby Last Circle shows ten tinted copies of each of five bodies.
gaps.recommendation: Do not generate ten more full rigs. Split each existing skin's albedo into 2-3 material zones (torso/legs/accent) so the wash can drive three independent colours instead of one, and add 3-4 attachment props parented to head/back bones (cap, helmet, backpack, mask) drawn from a small shared GLB. Five rigs x 3-colour zones x 4 attachments reads as dozens of distinct fighters for the cost of one small asset.

gaps.gap: The sky dome's faceted rim is visible over the ocean
gaps.evidence: maps.js: sky is SphereGeometry(SIZE * 0.82 = 1312, 24, 16) recentred on the camera each frame, while the water plane is PlaneGeometry(SIZE * 1.6 = 2560). In my Isla Viva aerial a large hard-edged pale-blue polygon silhouette floats on the horizon behind the volcano — the dome's lower rim reading against water that extends past it.
gaps.recommendation: Raise the dome radius above the water extent (SIZE * 1.4 or larger, still inside the 2000 m far plane once it is camera-centred) and raise segments to 32x24 so the gradient bands are not faceted. Then let the fog fix above dissolve the waterline into the dome so the seam stops mattering at all.

monetisation-readiness.verdict: Last Circle is a genuinely well-built game with essentially zero commercial plumbing: I grepped the entire game for `crazygames|sdk|adsbygoogle|gtag|analytics|rewarded|midgame|banner|sitelock` and got no hits in any code file, so there is no ad path, no gameplay-state signalling, no cloud save, no invite link, and no sitelock. The retention scaffolding that ad revenue actually depends on — an XP curve, 5 level-gated skins, a 7-field career record, a day streak, rotating challenges, and a menu-free PLAY AGAIN requeue — is already built and is the real asset here; what's missing is the ~300 lines of integration that turn those existing moments into billable events, plus two shell defects (a prohibited custom fullscreen button and a dead Pause button) that would fail portal QA on sight.

gaps.gap: The shell ships a custom fullscreen button, which CrazyGames explicitly prohibits — an automatic QA rejection independent of game quality
gaps.evidence: CrazyGames gameplay requirements state verbatim: "Custom in-game fullscreen buttons are prohibited." game_controls.js:196 builds `fs: _makeBtn("Fullscreen (F)", SVG.fsEnter, toggleFullscreen)` into an always-visible fixed bar, and :217 binds `KeyF` as a hotkey. index.html:12 loads that script with `window.GAME_CONFIG={hide_bug_button:true, mute_hotkey:false}` — the bug button is suppressed but the fullscreen button is not.
gaps.recommendation: game_controls.js:66 already honours `CFG.hide_controls === true` with an early return, and :217 already honours `CFG.fs_hotkey !== false`. For a portal build, set `hide_controls:true` in index.html's GAME_CONFIG (the portal supplies its own fullscreen chrome) and keep the current bar only for the self-hosted forgeflowgames.com build. Do this at the config layer so one index.html serves both targets.

gaps.gap: No portal SDK of any kind — which under CrazyGames' own tiering means ads are prohibited outright, not merely absent
gaps.evidence: grep -rniE "crazygames|sdk|adsbygoogle|gtag|analytics|advertis|midgame|rewarded|banner|preroll|sitelock" across every .js/.html/.json in the game returns zero code hits (only unrelated prose matches on the word "banner" in hud.js comments and "advertised" in player.js:383). CrazyGames docs state Basic implementation = `Gameplay start` event required, "ads prohibited"; Full implementation (gameplayStart/gameplayStop/sdkGameLoadingStart/sdkGameLoadingStop + Data + User) is what makes `ad.requestAd()` available.
gaps.recommendation: Add a thin `sdk.js` shim that no-ops when `getEnvironment()` returns 'local' or 'disabled', then wire ~8 call sites that already exist as distinct states: sdkGameLoadingStart/Stop around the buildMap+loadActorModels block (ffg_royale3d.js:250-295); gameplayStart in the `begin()` closure (ffg_royale3d.js:305); gameplayStop in showPostMatch (hud.js:2211), showSettings, showHowToPlay and togglePause; happytime() on the victory branch of showPostMatch (hud.js:2226) — the docs say use it sparingly, and VICTORY ROYALE is precisely the moment it exists for. This is the single item that gates every other monetisation item on this list.

gaps.gap: The always-visible Pause button is inert on every screen — window.__PAUSE__ is read but never assigned anywhere in the game
gaps.evidence: grep -rn "__PAUSE__" across the game returns exactly four lines, ALL inside game_controls.js: :17 (a comment), :199 `if (window.__PAUSE__ && window.__PAUSE__.toggle) window.__PAUSE__.toggle();`, and :229-230 in the leave-fullscreen auto-pause path. Nothing in runtime/ ever assigns it. Second-order consequence: the documented auto-pause on exiting fullscreen also silently no-ops, so pressing ESC out of fullscreen mid-firefight leaves the player standing in the open. hud.js already contains a complete togglePause(W) that nothing exports.
gaps.recommendation: In ffg_royale3d.js right after `hudMod.init(W)`, expose the bridge: `window.__PAUSE__ = { toggle: () => hudMod.requestPause(W), pause: () => hudMod.requestPause(W, true) };` and export a `requestPause` wrapper from hud.js that no-ops outside phase match/drop. One assignment makes ESC, the shell Pause button, and the fullscreen-exit hook all drive the same path — and gives you the gameplayStop call site you need anyway.

gaps.gap: Nothing to sell against a rewarded ad, and no midgame ad boundary declared — the two highest-RPM SDK surfaces have no design hook
gaps.evidence: The SDK exposes `ad.requestAd("rewarded", callbacks)` and `ad.requestAd("midgame", callbacks)`. Last Circle's post-match screen (hud.js:2211-2305) offers only PLAY AGAIN and MAIN MENU; there is no reward the player would trade 30 seconds of attention for. The XP economy that a reward would plug into is already there: match payout is computed at hud.js:2249-2253 and challenge XP at hud.js:1447-1450.
gaps.recommendation: Two placements, both of which respect the no-building / no-map-picker constraints because they are pure meta: (1) midgame ad fired on the PLAY AGAIN click before res.onAgain(), rate-limited to roughly one per 3 minutes of elapsed play so a 4-min Quick loop doesn't get double-served; (2) a rewarded ad on the post-match screen offering DOUBLE MATCH XP (reusing the `gained` value already computed at hud.js:2249) or a challenge-card reroll from CHAL_POOL. Both are cosmetic to the match itself — no competitive advantage sold, which keeps the game PEGI-12-clean and avoids pay-to-win complaints on a 50-bot lobby.

gaps.gap: Time-to-first-gameplay is at real risk against the ≤20s QA gate, and ~16s of it is self-inflicted fixed overhead
gaps.evidence: After the single mode-card click: showLobby fills 50 cells at 3-7 per 140ms tick (~1.4s) then runs a 3-count at 900ms intervals = ~4.1s of non-interactive cutscene (hud.js:930-957); then showDropSelect sets `let left = W.mode === "practice" ? 1 : 12;` (hud.js:1106) — a 12-second auto-lock. Concurrently loadActorModels preloads all 5 skins, and within each skin preloadMeshySkin loops `for (const clip of MESHY_CLIPS)` with an `await` inside (player.js:131-136), i.e. 8 SERIAL round trips per skin, 45 GLB fetches and 7.59MB total. Three.js also comes from cdn.jsdelivr.net (index.html importmap) on
gaps.recommendation: Three cheap wins, none of which touches game design: (1) Promise.all the 8 clip loads inside preloadMeshySkin instead of awaiting serially — same bytes, ~8x fewer round trips; (2) load only the player's chosen skin + 1 bot skin before the drop and stream the other 3 during the 12s drop-select, which is dead network time today; (3) cut the lobby fill tick from 140ms to ~60ms — the 50-name reveal reads the same at 0.6s as at 1.4s. Keep the 12s drop-select: it is genuine gameplay (you are reading heat numbers and choosing an LZ) and firing gameplayStart at its open makes it count as such.

gaps.gap: Zero integration with the portal's own already-built game bridge — leaderboards, achievements and cloud save exist and Last Circle uses none of them
gaps.evidence: src/lib/gameBridge.ts implements a postMessage receiver for `forgeflow:score`, `forgeflow:achievement` (by id OR slug), `forgeflow:level_complete`, `forgeflow:game_over` and `forgeflow:save`. grep -rln "forgeflow:" across games/ returns three integrators — cosmic-coils, nebula-drift-cosmic-predator, neon-veil — and Last Circle is not among them. No achievements are defined for last-circle in any supabase/migrations/*.sql. The bridge source even carries the comment "Good time for an interstitial ad" at the level_complete branch. Meanwhile Last Circle computes placement, kills, damage, accuracy,
gaps.recommendation: Emit `forgeflow:game_over` with a composite score on the post-match screen (hud.js:2211) and `forgeflow:achievement` on the milestones the code already detects — first win (res.victory), 5-kill game, level 3/6/10 skin unlocks (hud.js:2000 already fires on exactly those levels), 7-day streak. Mirror lc_progress via `forgeflow:save` so career survives a cleared cache. This is the difference between a career record that is a private number and one that is a competitive surface, and it is the one retention lever available before any external portal is involved.

gaps.gap: The unlock ladder is exhausted in roughly 27 matches, after which levelling pays nothing but a counter — and on an ad-funded game, post-ceiling retention IS the revenue
gaps.evidence: xpForLevel(lvl) = 800 + (lvl-1)*700 (hud.js:1187) → 32,400 XP to reach level 10, the last skin (hud.js:129, viper @ unlockLevel 10). A typical match pays 2 kills (200) + 400 damage (80) + placement 20 (180) + ~400s survived (100) = 560, plus up to 625 in challenge XP = ~1,185. That is ~27 matches, i.e. a few evenings. Past level 10 the menu falls back to `careerGoal(c)` (hud.js:140-144), which is a raw kill-count milestone with no reward attached — the code comment at :553 admits the goal slot previously vanished entirely for a maxed account.
gaps.recommendation: The cheapest high-yield extension that respects every hard constraint: attach unlockable weapon skins / tracer colours / kill-feed banners to levels 12-40 using the existing MENU_SKINS gating pattern, and make CHAL_POOL daily rather than per-match (the dayKey/dayStreak infrastructure at hud.js:1148-1172 already exists and is unused for anything but a streak counter). A daily-challenge reset is the standard reason a player opens a browser BR on day 2, and it is the exact surface a rewarded ad reroll monetises.

gaps.gap: Critical-path dependencies on third-party CDNs that neither the owner nor the portal controls
gaps.evidence: index.html's importmap resolves `three` to https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.172.0/build/three.module.js and `three/addons/` to the same host; runtime/net/ffg_netplay.js:41 does `await import("https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2")` at lobby-open time. CrazyGames requires relative paths for bundle files and evaluates externally-hosted files against the ≤20s-to-gameplay rule. A vendored copy already exists in the repo at forgeflow-games/three172.js. NOTE: this is a robustness/latency risk rather than a stated hard fail — Final Drop is itself listed as "Externally hosted (iframe)", so exter
gaps.recommendation: Vendor three.module.js and the two addons into assets/vendor/ and point the importmap at relative paths; pin and vendor supabase-js the same way (or lazy-load it only when SQUAD UP is clicked, which is already the case, so the risk there is contained to multiplayer). Removes a single point of failure on the loading path and takes the CDN latency out of the 20s budget.

gaps.gap: No player identity — the game never asks for a name, so the kill feed, the lobby and any future leaderboard all say "You"
gaps.evidence: `playerName: "You"` is a settings default at ffg_royale3d.js:420 but no UI writes it: the only `<input>` hud.js constructs is `inp.type = "range"` at hud.js:2510 (the volume sliders). net.js:117-119 works around the absence with `(W.settings.playerName && W.settings.playerName !== "You") ? ... : "Player-" + net.id.slice(-3)`. Meanwhile the game ships 68 hand-written bot names (sim/royale.js) so every opponent in the lobby has more identity than the player does.
gaps.recommendation: Add one `<input maxlength=16>` at the top of showSettings (hud.js:2192) bound to W.settings.playerName, plus the same field on the SQUAD UP panel — net.js:98 already builds an input there for the room code, so the styling exists. player.js already ignores keydown when ev.target is an INPUT, so typing will not drive the character. This is a prerequisite for any leaderboard being meaningful.

gaps.gap: Shareability is effectively zero — the room code is unselectable text and a victory produces nothing a player can send anyone
gaps.evidence: net.js:130 ends the lobby flow at `Room ${net.room} — share this code.` with no copy button; grep for `clipboard` across the game returns nothing; grep for `share|twitter|copy` in hud.js returns only unrelated matches. game_controls.js:65 additionally blocks the context menu page-wide with `capture:true`, so a player cannot even right-click-copy the code. The SDK provides showInviteButton({roomId})/inviteLink({roomId})/getInviteParam() built for exactly this, and the docs specify hiding the invite button once the room is full or the match has started.
gaps.recommendation: Wire showInviteButton({roomId: net.room}) when the lobby opens and hideInviteButton() in the `begin()` closure at ffg_royale3d.js:305 (the docs require hiding it at gameplay start); read getInviteParam('roomId') on boot to auto-join. As a portal-independent fallback, add a copy-to-clipboard button next to the code in net.js and a share card on VICTORY ROYALE. In a 50-bot lobby the friend-invite is the main organic acquisition channel and it currently depends on a player typing a code they read aloud.

gaps.gap: No sitelock, which CrazyGames requires
gaps.evidence: CrazyGames technical requirements: "Implement sitelock to prevent file theft" and "Whitelist all CrazyGames domains if using sitelock." grep for `sitelock|domain|location.hostname|referrer` across the game's code returns no domain check anywhere.
gaps.recommendation: Add a hostname allowlist check in ffg_boot3d.js before boot3d() — permit localhost/127.0.0.1, forgeflowgames.com, the R2 origin, and the crazygames.com / crazygames.* domains, and bail with a message otherwise. Keep the list in one place; a sitelock that is hard to update becomes the reason a legitimate portal build refuses to run.

gaps.gap: No in-game analytics — you cannot measure whether any monetisation change helped or hurt
gaps.evidence: The portal has GA4 (pages/+Head.tsx:14, G-Z1R90RFQKP) and a `play_count` column ordered on in src/hooks/useGames.ts, but those are page-level. Inside the game nothing records menu→match conversion, drop-select abandonment, matches per session, average placement, or day-2 return. The data all exists in memory: W.match tracks kills/damage/placement, W.progress tracks matches/wins/dayStreak.
gaps.recommendation: Emit a handful of events at the boundaries you are already instrumenting for the SDK (loading start/stop, gameplay start/stop, post-match) to GA4 via the parent frame or a 20-line beacon. The specific numbers to watch before touching ad frequency: matches per session, and the drop-off between menu-shown and first-match-started. Without these, an ad placement that costs you 15% of session length is invisible.

gaps.gap: Desktop-only: no touch input anywhere, forfeiting the mobile homepage and roughly a third of US portal traffic
gaps.evidence: grep for `touchstart|touchmove|ontouch|maxTouchPoints|joystick|orientation` across runtime/ and game_controls.js returns no input handlers (only unrelated hits on the word "orientation" in player.js's bone-rotation comments). CrazyGames requires ≤20MB initial download for mobile-homepage eligibility. HONEST CONTEXT: Final Drop is itself listed as "Browser (desktop-only)" and rates 9.2/10, and Similarweb puts CrazyGames US traffic at ~65% desktop — so this is parity with the primary benchmark, not a deficit against it.
gaps.recommendation: Do NOT build touch controls to chase this — a 50-player third-person shooter with ADS, six weapons, chest-holds and a parachute does not survive twin-stick translation, and Final Drop's rating proves desktop-only is viable. Instead, detect touch at boot and show an honest "desktop only" card rather than letting a phone user load 8MB of GLB and then discover they cannot move. That is a one-screen change and it protects the rating, which is what portal placement actually keys off.

gaps.gap: 3.6MB of unreferenced backup files shipped in the bundle, and 15MB of music at a bitrate that looks unnecessary for looping tracks
gaps.evidence: Five `.openhands.bak` files totalling 3,790,564 bytes (juggernaut 820,244; athlete 789,888; wraith 766,152; soldier 711,308; viper 702,972) sit in assets/chars/meshy/; grep for "openhands" across all .js/.json/.html returns no code reference. The three MP3s total 15,681,306 bytes (14.95MB) for looping background tracks.
gaps.recommendation: Delete the .bak files from the shipped tree (keep them in git history if wanted) and re-encode the music at a lower bitrate — these are looping ambient beds, not a soundtrack album. Neither threatens the 250MB cap, but both directly reduce the initial-download figure that the portal measures and the total the CDN serves on every cold load.

performance.verdict: Last Circle's simulation layer is genuinely excellent — 50 actors with AI, movement, ballistics, loot and storm cost 0.55 ms/frame — and its load footprint (16.8 MB to first playable match, 112 files) sits comfortably inside every CrazyGames hard limit, but the renderer wastes roughly 60% of its frame on geometry that is provably invisible: on Deepwood a ground camera submits 763 draw calls and 3,716,659 triangles, of which 505 calls and ~7.3 ms are loot pickups at a median distance of 1,132 m. Frustum culling is structurally disabled (all 30 InstancedMeshes have bounding radii of 850–1,011 m on a 1,600 m map; pointing the camera at empty sky still submits 2,901,932 triangles), and the frame is entirely CPU/draw-call bound — rendering at 64×36 costs the same as 1280×720 — which means the DPR-and-shadow-resolution quality tiers are aimed at a bottleneck that does not exist.

gaps.gap: Ground loot is rendered at unlimited distance — it is the single largest cost in the frame and roughly two thirds of all draw calls
gaps.evidence: Deepwood ground view: 763 draw calls / 3,716,659 tris / 12.6 ms. Hiding W._groups.loot: 258 calls / 5.33 ms. Loot = 505 draw calls and ~7.3 ms (14.4 us per call). Of the 134 top-level loot groups, the median distance from the camera was 1,132 m and the farthest 1,947 m; a 150 m cull left only 2 visible. Each item is a Group holding a rarity torus plus a cloned Meshy model (item_medkit 5,919 tris, wpn_sniper 6,143, wpn_glauncher 6,169) and each sub-mesh is its own draw call. Three.js only frustum-tests the leaf meshes, and with a 2,000 m far plane on a 1,600 m map the frustum contains most of t
gaps.recommendation: In loot.js update(), toggle group.visible on a squared-distance test against the camera each frame (or every 4th frame over a rotating slice) with a cut at ~150 m. Measured effect on the exact frame profiled: 763 -> 258 draw calls, 12.6 -> 5.33 ms, a 2.4x render speedup for a few lines. Then add a cheap far tier — keep only the rarity ring, or a single additive billboard sprite, out to ~400 m so loot is still spottable from a rooftop without paying for a 6,000-triangle rifle.

gaps.gap: Frustum culling is structurally disabled for every large object in the world
gaps.evidence: Measured bounding-sphere radii: terrain 1,131 m, roads 603 m, and all 30 InstancedMeshes between 850 m and 1,011 m — on a 1,600 m map with camera.far = 2,000 and FOV 57. Every one of these intersects the frustum from anywhere on the map. Proof of the consequence: with the camera pointed straight up at empty sky the renderer still submitted 2,901,932 triangles. Merged structure batches are keyed by colour hex globally, so one 'grey concrete' batch spans the whole island and is submitted whenever any grey building is on screen.
gaps.recommendation: Chunk spatially. In maps.js, bucket each prop kind's instance list into an 8x8 grid of 200 m cells and emit one InstancedMesh per (kind, primitive, cell) — bounding radius drops from ~1,000 m to ~140 m and culling starts working, at a modest increase in object count that is more than repaid. Do the same for the structure batches: key `batches` by (colour, POI) instead of colour alone, since POIs are already the natural spatial cluster. Consider three.js BatchedMesh as the alternative if you want per-object culling inside a single draw call.

gaps.gap: Kernel3D.loadGLTF has no in-flight request dedupe, so concurrent loads of the same asset each allocate their own copy of its textures
gaps.evidence: Direct test in the running game: five concurrent kernel.loadGLTF() calls on one uncached URL produced 5 distinct THREE.Source objects; five sequential calls on the now-warm URL produced 1. Consequence in a live match: the scene holds 202 unique texture Sources while the GLTF/character caches hold only 46 — 156 duplicates. 143 of the live sources are 512x512, giving ~200 MB of estimated texture memory where ~65 MB would suffice. The loot group alone holds 134 unique sources and the actor group 57 (for 5 distinct skins). ffg_kernel_3d.js:251 checks `this._gltfCache[url]` before the await but nev
gaps.recommendation: Add an `_gltfInflight` map: on miss, store the loadAsync promise before awaiting, have subsequent callers await the same promise, and delete the entry when it settles. Same three lines in loadCharacter. This is a generator-level fix in the shared FFG kernel, so it pays out across every 3D game in the portal, and it is the difference between ~200 MB and ~65 MB of texture residency on the 4 GB Chromebooks CrazyGames explicitly requires you to run on.

gaps.gap: The quality tiers scale the wrong axis — the frame is CPU/draw-call bound, not fill bound, so the settings menu barely moves frame rate
gaps.evidence: Rendering the same view at 64x36 took 3.54 ms versus 3.33 ms at 1280x720 — eliminating 99.9% of the pixels changed nothing. Resolution sweep at fixed content: 1280x720 DPR1 10.9 ms, 1280x720 DPR1.5 11.24 ms, 1920x1080 DPR1 15.54 ms, 1920x1080 DPR1.5 18.41 ms — a 5x pixel increase for 1.7x the time. Tier sweep on ashgrid: high (DPR 2.0, shadow 4096) 319 calls / 4.06 ms, medium (DPR 1.5, 2048) 318 / 3.92 ms, low (DPR 1.0, no shadows, no bloom) 276 / 3.08 ms. The tier tables in ffg_royale3d.js:100-158 control DPR, shadow map size, anisotropy and bloom — none of which is the bottleneck.
gaps.recommendation: Re-target the tiers at draw-call count once gaps 1 and 2 land. Make each tier own: loot cull radius (low 90 m / medium 150 m / high 250 m), prop instance-chunk draw distance, foliage density multiplier applied at scatterTrees time, actor model LOD switch distance, and whether distant actors drop to a single low-poly mesh. Keep DPR as a secondary knob for genuinely GPU-poor integrated parts, but stop presenting it as the main lever.

gaps.gap: The heaviest frame in the entire match is the very first one the player sees, and there is no character or held-weapon LOD
gaps.evidence: With the camera at the 50-actor drop cluster: 1,010 draw calls, 4,456,503 triangles, 17.77 ms render-only — ~56 FPS before any game logic, on a discrete RTX A2000. The actor group holds 1,039,140 triangles across 100 meshes, i.e. ~20,800 tris per actor: a 12,761–15,636 triangle Meshy body plus a ~6,000 triangle held weapon that is full detail whether the holder is 3 m or 400 m away. Animation LOD exists (mixers freeze past 250 m, player.js:647/979) but there is no geometry LOD at any distance.
gaps.recommendation: Two steps, cheapest first. (a) Swap the held weaponMesh for a ~200-triangle proxy beyond ~60 m — weapons.js already builds procedural box-primitive protos (protos.smg/sniper/glauncher) as GLB fallbacks, so the low-detail asset already exists; wire it as an LOD instead of a fallback. That alone removes ~300k triangles from the drop frame. (b) Generate one decimated body LOD per skin (target ~2,500 tris) and use THREE.LOD at ~80 m. Decimation can be a one-off offline step, not runtime.

gaps.gap: Tree instances always cast shadows and, being uncullable, run the shadow depth pass over the whole map's foliage every frame
gaps.evidence: Toggling shadowMap.enabled on the Deepwood ground view moved triangles 3,716,659 -> 2,379,359, i.e. the depth pass costs 1,337,300 triangles/frame — which matches the pine (943,605) plus birch (344,208) instanced totals almost exactly. Both InstancedMeshes have castShadow=true and radii of ~1,000 m, so the +/-55 m shadow camera can never reject them; every tree on a 1,600 m map is re-rendered into a 55 m shadow box every frame. maps.js:1223-1229 already documents this exact reasoning for why cars, barrels and rocks had their castShadow turned off — trees were deliberately exempted.
gaps.recommendation: This is fixed for free by the chunked instancing in gap 2: once each foliage chunk has a ~140 m radius, the shadow frustum rejects all but the two or three chunks actually inside the +/-55 m box. If chunking slips, the interim fix is to maintain a small castShadow-enabled InstancedMesh rebuilt with only the ~40 nearest trees each time the player crosses a 20 m threshold, with the map-wide mesh set castShadow=false.

gaps.gap: Pickup and item models are AAA-hero-prop density for objects that are usually a few pixels on screen
gaps.evidence: Parsed from the GLBs: item_bandage 5,963 tris, item_medkit 5,919, item_shield_s 5,472, item_shield_l 6,126, wpn_ar 5,943, wpn_smg 5,962, wpn_pistol 5,955, wpn_shotgun 6,088, wpn_sniper 6,143, wpn_glauncher 6,169, deco_crystal 5,939 — every Meshy asset lands in a 5.5k–6.2k band with 3–4 512x512 PBR maps each. For comparison the hand-authored props in the same folder are 308 (barrel), 314 (rocks), 364 (bush), 1,681 (pine) triangles.
gaps.recommendation: Run the Meshy outputs through a one-off decimation pass (gltf-transform simplify or Blender decimate) targeting ~800–1,200 triangles for pickups and ~2,000 for the held-weapon LOD0, and drop their texture sets to 256x256 for the 3 non-albedo maps. A bandage on the ground does not need a 512x512 roughness map. Combined with the loot distance cull this compounds: fewer triangles AND fewer of them submitted.

gaps.gap: Match build blocks the main thread for ~1.9 s with no incremental progress, and shader compilation adds a first-encounter hitch
gaps.evidence: Measured warm per-match build (all GLBs cached): 1,934 ms of frozen main thread. A Node replication of the pure noise work — 221x221 terrain vertices plus the 512x512 minimap, both calling the 5-octave fbm height function and colorAt — accounted for 39.8 ms and 90.9 ms respectively on this CPU, so the remaining ~1.8 s is geometry construction, mergeGeometries and GLTF/instancing work. Separately, shader programs went 0 -> 86 during match 1 before settling at 59, meaning the first match compiles ~86 programs on demand. There is a single `await nextFrame()` before buildMap and nothing after it.
gaps.recommendation: Still inside CrazyGames' 20 s time-to-gameplay budget on this hardware, but on the 4 GB Chromebooks they gate on this is likely 4–6 s of a hard-frozen tab per match, repeated on every PLAY AGAIN. Yield to the event loop between build phases (terrain, structures, props, loot) so the loading screen can animate, move the 512x512 minimap raster into a Worker or an OffscreenCanvas since nothing depends on it until the HUD appears, and call renderer.compile(scene, camera) once during the lobby to move shader compilation into a moment the player already expects to wait.
